Definition: from πτώσσω (to crouch); akin to G4422 and the alternate of G4098); a beggar (as cringing), i.e. pauper (strictly denoting absolute or public mendicancy, although also used in a qualified or relative sense; whereas G3993 properly means only straitened circumstances in private), literally (often as noun) or figuratively (distressed):--beggar(-ly), poor.
BiblicalUsage: Ptochos means poor, a beggar, one who crouches for alms. Jesus says, Blessed are the poor in spirit, for theirs is the kingdom of heaven, and, Blessed be ye poor, for yours is the kingdom of God. He came to preach the gospel to the poor. And He said, The poor always ye have with you, but Me ye have not always.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe the poor are blessed, not because poverty is good, but because the poor know they need God and the rich forget. I hold that the gospel came to the poor first, and the kingdom belongs to those who know they have nothing to bring.
